links.anchor: -43% violent-crime arrests over 16 months, mostly after the program

research.result: Author abstract: 43% fewer violent-crime arrests over 16 months; 3.95 fewer arrests per 100 assigned youth.
research.breadth: Randomized assignment of 1634 disadvantaged Chicago high-school youth to an eight-week program; mostly post-program decline.
research.access: Author abstract read.
research.missingFigure: Need assignment-effect interval, eligible-youth denominator, program take-up, and the slot-to-assignment mapping. A raw extra slot is not a 43% reduction for the whole place, and assignment is not treatment received.

links.anchor: More guilty pleas and convictions

research.result: Table 4 fully controlled 2SLS: release -0.156 probability points, SE 0.034; detained mean 0.571.
research.breadth: Marginal defendants affected by randomly assigned bail judges in Philadelphia and Miami-Dade; release versus detention.
research.access: Working paper full text and Table 4 read.
research.missingFigure: Need the final AER table interval, conviction baseline among the affected marginal defendants, and a defined detention input unit. Reversing a release effect and dividing by the whole detained mean does not establish the effect of detention on every defendant.

links.anchor: Lower formal employment afterward

research.result: Table 7 fully controlled 2SLS: release +0.037 employment probability points (SE 0.043) in years 1 to 2, +0.102 (SE 0.053) in years 3 to 4.
research.breadth: Same marginal defendant population; tax-record formal employment, not all work.
research.access: Working paper full text and Table 7 read.
research.missingFigure: Need final published estimates and intervals, affected-defendant employment baseline, and distinct follow-up exposure records. The first-period imprecise estimate is not evidence of zero; a single immediate lag cannot represent both periods.

links.anchor: Reduces youth firearm suicide, injuries and homicide (RAND: supportive)
links.source: RAND Science of Gun Policy, 5th ed.

research.result: RAND fifth-edition review: supportive evidence of reductions in youth firearm suicides, homicides or assault injuries, and unintentional injuries/deaths for specified child-access laws.
research.breadth: Definitions distinguish storage/child-access and reckless-provision laws; age and outcome definitions vary.
research.access: Current RAND policy review read.
research.missingFigure: Need matched law-definition estimates and intervals separately for youth suicide, homicide and unintentional death, with ages and follow-up. Evidence grades supply no pooled numeric range for a combined youth gun-death outcome.

links.group: state population; pooled 41-state study, not an individual death probability
links.anchor: Monthly firearm-homicide IRR 1.08 (95% CI 1.03 to 1.13); observational national pooled model, 1999 to 2017.
links.source: RAND Science of Gun Policy, 5th ed.; Degli Esposti et al. 2022, JAMA Network Open, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2022.0077; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8861849/

research.result: Firearm-homicide IRR 1.08, 95% CI 1.03 to 1.13; main national model, Results.
research.breadth: 41 states, 23 statutory adopters and 18 controls, 1999 to 2017; monthly state rates. Observational controlled interrupted time series, not randomized. State associations differ.
research.access: Full article and RAND review read.
research.conversion: size = IRR - 1; range = published main-model 95% IRR interval minus 1. This interval measures pooled-estimate uncertainty, not variation across states.
research.transportLimit: Study excluded nine states and does not establish effects for territories, townships, newer enactments, repeal, or preempted local rules. State variation can exceed this pooled interval. No legal authority is inferred.
research.readerStatus: No person feels this yet: no cause or outcome reader was verified in this research batch. A numeric entry is not runtime activation proof.

links.anchor: Raising the minimum age reduces youth firearm suicide (RAND: supportive)
links.source: RAND Science of Gun Policy, 5th ed.

research.result: RAND fifth-edition review: supportive evidence that minimum purchasing-age laws reduce youth firearm suicide.
research.breadth: Purchasing versus possession ages and covered firearm types are distinct; youth age definitions differ.
research.access: Current RAND policy review read.
research.missingFigure: Need the specific age transition, firearm coverage, youth age band, reported suicide estimate and interval, and lag. A generic minimum-age yes/no does not identify the treatment whose size was studied.

links.per: one percentage-point increase in TSP concentration relative to place start; local linear elasticity approximation near start
links.group: infant birth cohorts exposed to TSP; internal-cause deaths per live births
links.anchor: IV elasticity 0.45; reported design/subsample elasticity spread 0.3 to 0.7. Per pct-of-start point divide each elasticity by 100.
links.source: Chay and Greenstone 2003, Air Quality, Infant Mortality, and the Clean Air Act of 1970, NBER w10053, pp.20-21,26-27; https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w10053/w10053.pdf

research.result: Page 26: inverse-sampling-error-weighted IV elasticity 0.45. Pages 20 to 21 report 0.3 to 0.6; page 27 reports 0.6 to 0.7 near the regulatory cutoff.
research.breadth: US monitored counties, 1971 to 1972 changes induced by Clean Air Act nonattainment. TSP, not PM2.5 or an air-quality index. Outcome is internal-cause infant deaths per live births.
research.access: Working paper full text and tables read.
research.conversion: size = 0.45 / 100; range = [0.3 / 100, 0.7 / 100]. The cause is percent of starting TSP, so a one-point increase gives a 0.45% local proportional mortality increase.
research.transportLimit: Study specification/subsample spread is not a CI or modern PM2.5 coefficient. Requires TSP-specific cause and infant internal-cause outcome readers; neither was verified. No supported general air-quality-index conversion.
research.readerStatus: No person feels this yet: no cause or outcome reader was verified in this research batch. A numeric entry is not runtime activation proof.

links.anchor: Cleaner air at birth: higher earnings and work at 30

research.result: Table 4: ten-microgram-per-cubic-meter TSP increase yields -186.21 to -351.74 annual earnings dollars across specifications; log-earnings coefficients -0.005 to -0.014.
research.breadth: Birth cohorts 1969 to 1974 in 148 counties; earnings ages 29 to 31; Clean Air Act IV.
research.access: Working paper full text and Table 4 read.
research.missingFigure: Need final JPE estimates, earnings price year and matching cohort mean for the annual-earnings outcome, plus birth-year TSP units and exposure record. Log earnings and mean annual earnings are different estimands; the log coefficients cannot silently replace the annual-earnings outcome.

links.anchor: Nonattainment rules cut particulates

research.result: Table 5 nonattainment coefficients on TSP change: -11.9, -11.0, -10.0, -8.8, -8.9, -6.3 micrograms per cubic meter across specifications.
research.breadth: 1972 nonattainment designated using 1970 TSP relative to the federal ceiling; US monitored counties, one-year change.
research.access: Correct Chay and Greenstone working paper and Table 5 read.
research.missingFigure: Need exposed-place initial TSP concentration and actual nonattainment eligibility/enforcement to convert the absolute concentration change into a proportional outcome factor. A general emissions law is not automatically this designation. No invented national percentage cut.

links.anchor: Medicaid nearly eliminated bills over 30% of income

links.anchor: RAND: looser (shall-issue) carry laws raise total and firearm homicides; requiring a permit is the other way
links.source: RAND Science of Gun Policy, 5th ed.

research.result: RAND fifth-edition review: supportive evidence that shall-issue laws increase firearm homicides; permitless and may-issue rules are distinct comparisons.
research.breadth: US state laws with different issuance and eligibility rules.
research.access: Current RAND policy review read.
research.missingFigure: Need the exact permitting transition and firearm-homicide estimate/interval for that comparison. A permit-required boolean combines shall-issue and may-issue laws; simply reversing a shall-issue estimate would misidentify the treatment.
